# FDG9159

> CONSIDER naming an `out` parameter that reports the number of values written by a buffer-writing method “bytesWritten,” “charsWritten,” or “valuesWritten” (as appropriate to the data type).

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 9.12.1 Data Transformation Operations.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG9159
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library suggestion, application suggestion, test none
- Status: draft

Message: Name the out parameter '{0}' of '{1}' '{2}'

FDG9159 reports the out parameter that reports the number of values written by an externally visible buffer-writing method when its name is not the one for the element type of the destination: bytesWritten for byte and sbyte, charsWritten for char, valuesWritten for any other type. The parameter is found in two shapes: the only out parameter of an integer type of a Try-Write method (named Try followed by an uppercase letter, returning bool, with a parameter named destination of type Span<T>, Memory<T>, an array or ArraySegment<T>), and the written one of exactly two such out parameters of a method that returns OperationStatus and has an output buffer (found as for FDG9173): the second, or the first when it ends with Written and the second with Consumed. A byte output buffer counted by charsWritten is not reported: the ToBase64 example of FDG9174 writes Base64 text to a Span<byte> and names the parameter so. Other buffer-writing methods, overrides and interface implementations are not checked, so coverage is partial. Renaming a public parameter breaks callers that pass it as a named argument, so the fix is breaking; there is no code fix.

## From the book

One simple example of this pattern is the `TryFormat` method on `System.Version`:

```csharp
public bool TryFormat(
  Span<char> destination, out int charsWritten) { ... }
```
